messages:
maria.g: Quick question — audit export access model. Customers keep asking: who can read tenant audit streams? specifically: org admins vs project members. We need a clear RBAC + schema story for customer-facing exports. Thoughts?

jess: Are we talking hosted only or private deployments too?

maria.g: Both. Hosted needs policy + UI controls. Private should be able to opt into the same filtering + KMS signing behaviors.

trevor.k: Proposal sketch: introduce scoped audit tokens + explicit 'audit.read' scopes. Token claim example: aud=\"tenant:abc123\" scope=\"audit.read\" role=\"admin|member\". Audit-reader/enrichment service enforces token tenant claim and role-based redaction. Also add fields to schema: actor_role, actor_display_role, audit_schema_v.

alex_p: Keep it additive. Many customers pipe events into SIEMs that expect stable fields — do not break existing keys. Instead: versioned export wrapper and include events array. 

security-qa-bot: Flag from vuln triage: aggregated events leaked tenant_display_name in metadata when multiple tenants were combined. We should redact or hash display names when cross-tenant export is enabled.

maria.g: Agreed. For customer-facing exports we should: 1) remove PII, 2) replace display names with tenant-scoped IDs, or 3) hash tenant_id with a salt. Also add per-batch signature so customers can verify authenticity (KMS-based).

trevor.k: On signing: prefer per-batch signature (sign batch root) instead of per-event to save perf. Implementation options: HSM-signed RSA signature using platform KMS for hosted, and allow customer-managed KMS (CMK) for private/dedicated. Expose JWKS or cert to customers for verification. Access to signing keys must itself be RBAC-gated.

jess: How will SIEMs validate? Provide a JWKS endpoint + batch metadata: batch_id, created_at, signer_kid, signature. Example wrapper: 

```json
{
  "audit_schema_v": "2",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_abc123",
  "batch_id": "b-20240501-0001",
  "batch_signature": "sig_base64...",
  "events": [ /* v1-compatible events here */ ]
}
```

alex_p: Migration plan points: dual-write exports for a period, readers accept v1 payloads and v2 wrappers. Add header X-Audit-Schema-Version for streaming endpoints. Avoid breaking existing parsers.

trevor.k: RBAC nuance: split permission into audit.read:full and audit.read:redacted. Admins get full, members get redacted. Enforce both at authn layer and again at export service to prevent privilege escalation via scoped tokens. Attribute-based policies (tenant_id match + role) are easiest to reason about.

security-qa-bot: Tests to add:
- E2E where member token attempts to fetch other-tenant events -> 403.
- Export wrapper signature verification test using platform KMS mock.
- Redaction smoke: ensure display_name removed in redacted payloads.

sre-bot: deploy: audit-export-service v2 rolled to staging @1728460000 :white_check_mark:

maria.g: Perf question: signing per-batch + large batches? alex_p?

alex_p: If batches > 100k events, sign Merkle root. For typical batches (<=10k) signing root is fine. Cache CMK auth to avoid per-batch authlatency. Also add streaming option where events are gzipped and chunk-signed.

jess: Implementation owners? I can take export UI + docs. trevor.k will own authz changes. alex_p will own perf/migration plan. security-qa will own tests. maria.g will draft RFC with examples and migration timeline.

maria.g: Action items:
- I’ll kick off RFC with schema examples, sample JWT claims and migration runbook.
- @trevor.k to draft policy rules (audit.read:full, audit.read:redacted).
- @jess to mock SIEM verification docs and JWKS examples.
- @alex_p to benchmark signing strategies and recommend thresholds.
- @security-qa-bot to add E2E tests to CI.

trevor.k: One more: we should avoid exposing internal tenant mapping keys in logs. Any reader path that returns tenant mapping must require additional scope: mapping.read.

maria.g: Good call. I’ll add mapping.read to the RFC. Thanks all — I’ll post the RFC link once ready. :eyes:
